points.quote: `Workbench` (`modules/workbench/entities/workbench.ts`) is the window manager. It holds `views$`, `activeViewIndex$`, an `activeView$` and the right-sidebar state.
Each `View` (`entities/view.ts`) is one pane in a split-view layout (`view/split-view/`) and is created by the workbench. ... `workbench-root.tsx` lays the views out side by side.
It has its own `scope`, its own history and a `location$` derived from that history. ... exposes `backable` and `forwardable`.
Each view renders through `ViewRoot` ... It creates a private `createMemoryRouter(routes)`, subscribes to `view.location$`, and calls `viewRouter.navigate(location)`
A route component doesn't draw its own chrome. It renders `ViewHeader`, `ViewBody` and `ViewSidebarTab` (`view/view-islands.tsx`). ... They look up the island by id and portal the content in.
The active view's URL counts as the URL of the whole app.
It shows only the active view's sidebar tabs. If a view has several tabs, a header switcher (`sidebar-header-switcher.tsx`) lets the user choose between them.
In a browser, `browser-adapter.ts` ... pushes the active view's location into the browser URL. It also passes the browser's back and forward navigation to the active view.
